text.p: Thermatrix Inc Friday said it recently received an order from the U.S. Department of the Navy worth $900,000 and has begun engineering work on three commercial systems for U.S. customers worth another $1.7 million.
In a statement accompanying its first quarter financial results the company said it has also resumed work on a large commercial system $2 million contract which was delayed for three months.

Earlier, the company reported it lost $2 million, or $0.26 per share, in the first quarter of fiscal 1997, compared with a net loss of $1.2 million, or $0.22 per share, in the first quarter of fiscal 1996. Revenues for the first quarter of fiscal 1997 were $1.1 million, down from the $2.7 million recorded in the comparable quarter in the prior year.

John Schofield, chairman, president and chief executive, attributed the lower than expected revenue figures to the postponement of one order by a customer, a three-month delay of a significant order by another customer, and the cancellation of orders by two other customers after engineering work had already been completed.

In addition, nine projects were in the final stages of installation and commissioning during the quarter. The company said seven of the nine systems have been completed and are in full operation, and the remaining two should complete commissioning in the second quarter.
In addition, the company said test results from the Formatrix joint venture prototype unit for the pre-treatment of radioactive mixed wastes have exceeded expectations.
